source_title: Motorola finally puts a date on its Galaxy Ultra challenger
source_excerpt:

Motorola has officially confirmed that the Signature 27 will launch on November 5.
The phone’s US landing page is live, showcasing its premium design and flagship hardware.
A Geekbench listing reveals more performance details, but pricing remains under wraps.
The original Motorola Signature had the looks and the hardware to rub shoulders with Android’s finest, but American buyers never got an invitation. Its successor is rewriting that script. It first made a cheeky appearance on Motorola’s US website, then debuted at Snapdragon Summit, putting the Galaxy Ultra and Pixel Pro on notice. Now, the Signature 27 has a date with America, and it’s just days away.
Motorola has officially confirmed November 5 as the launch date for the Signature 27. In a new X teaser, the company highlights the phone’s premium design and comfortable ergonomics and invites fans to see it next Thursday.
The Signature 27’s US landing page is also live, featuring a slick promotional video that highlights its distinctive camera island and premium finishes. Motorola proudly bills it as its most advanced smartphone yet, and the hardware backs up that claim.
Underneath that polished exterior sits Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, paired with Motorola’s elaborate ArcticMesh cooling system. Photography gets equally ambitious treatment, with a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main sensor and a whopping 200MP periscope telephoto camera. Bang & Olufsen-tuned audio completes the flagship package.
Meanwhile, the Signature 27 has already flexed its silicon on Geekbench (via AndroidTreasure ), posting 3,313 single-core and 11,088 multi-core points. The listing also reveals Android 17 and 12GB of RAM.
However, all that flagship firepower could burn a sizable hole in your wallet. A recent European retailer leak pointed to a €1,594.90 price tag — roughly $1,773 — although Motorola hasn’t confirmed US pricing. November 5 should bring more clarity, including whether Americans can actually buy the phone immediately.
Motorola has already made its case on paper. Now it needs to prove the Signature 27 is more than a beautifully dressed spec monster, especially if it wants US buyers to look past their Galaxies and Pixels.
